_comment: The starting state of a demo playoff night: every league seeded from seed-config.json, then courts assigned exactly as the venue's own bracket PDFs schedule them. This is the 6:30pm wave of Tuesday 15 September 2026 (R3-26) -- eleven matches on their real courts, one court per match, no clashes. Court 1 is idle because the brackets do not use it at 6:30.
_whyNotEveryCourt: The 7:00pm matches are deliberately left unassigned. Every one of them is scheduled onto a court the 6:30 wave is still using (Coed 4s A 1v8 wants court 2, where 4v5 is playing), so at the moment this night starts they are genuinely waiting for a court -- which is what the controller's 'needs a court' queue is for. An earlier version of this file filled all twelve courts round-robin, which looked busier and described a night nobody was running.
_noTimes: Times are documented here and nowhere else on purpose: the event log has no concept of a match time. A playoff night does not run to a clock -- the coordinator assigns a court when one frees up -- so the PDF's times inform WHICH matches start on court, and are not data the system stores.
_sharedBy: prototype/tools/demo-playoff-night.sh (native server, via curl) and prototype/demo.html (browser wasm build). Edit here, not in either consumer.
_source: reference/brackets/Tuesday-*-Playoffs-R3-26*.pdf -- the venue's own brackets. Match ids are this engine's, resolved from the PDF's seed pairings.
